cards.text: Then the prophet Ezekiel says the word of the LORD came to him on the first day of the eleventh month of the twelfth year. God calls him "Son of man" and gives him a message about the city of Tyre. Tyre has been talking about Jerusalem, and God heard every word.

cards.question: Jerusalem lies in ruins. How does the city of Tyre react?

answers.text: It gloats and expects to gain
It panics and shuts its gates

cards.text: Tyre says, "Aha! The gate to the nations is broken; it has swung open to me; now that she lies in ruins I will be filled". That's the coworker who hears you got let go and asks, "So who gets your parking spot?"

cards.question: True or false: After Tyre's "Aha!" over Jerusalem, God says He is on Tyre's side.

cards.text: God says, "Behold, O Tyre, I am against you". He'll raise up many nations against Tyre, as the sea brings up its waves.

cards.question: The nations that roll in against Tyre like waves will ___ her walls and towers.

cards.text: And God isn't stopping at the walls. He says, "I will scrape the soil from her and make her a bare rock."

cards.question: Once Tyre is a bare rock in the sea, God says it will become a place to spread ___.

cards.text: Tyre becomes plunder for the nations, and the villages on her mainland are slain by the sword.

cards.question: God says that after all this happens to Tyre, "they will know" something. What will they know?
Which king is God bringing against Tyre from the north?

cards.text: God calls Nebuchadnezzar king of kings, and he's bringing horses, chariots, cavalry and a great company of troops. Friend, that's the whole stadium parking lot pulling out at ONCE.
Nebuchadnezzar slaughters the villages of Tyre's mainland with the sword. Then he sets up siege works, builds a ramp to her walls and raises his shields against her.

cards.question: Nebuchadnezzar's ramp reaches Tyre's walls and his shields are up. What does he aim at those walls?

cards.text: Battering rams on the walls, axes on the towers, and his horses kick up so much dust it covers the city.

cards.question: True or false: When Nebuchadnezzar rides through Tyre's gates, the walls shake from the noise.

cards.text: Cavalry, wagons and chariots, all rattling those walls. I know that rattle, friend, because every time somebody yanked my junk drawer open I shook just like that, and they were only looking for tape.
The hooves of his horses trample every street, and he slaughters Tyre's people with the sword.

cards.question: True or false: As Nebuchadnezzar's horses trample Tyre's streets, her mighty pillars stay standing.
Nebuchadnezzar's army plunders Tyre's wealth and tears down her walls and beautiful homes. Where do they throw the stones, timber and soil?

cards.text: They don't pile it up and they don't haul it off, friend. They throw it all in the WATER.

cards.question: As Tyre falls apart, God says He will silence the sound of Tyre's ___.
True or false: God says Tyre will be rebuilt someday.

cards.text: God says Tyre will never be rebuilt, "for I, the LORD, have spoken". When He says it, friend, there's no second draft.
Then God speaks to Tyre about how the coastlands will take the news. "Will not the coastlands quake at the sound of your downfall, when the wounded groan at the slaughter in your midst?"

cards.question: Tyre falls and the coastlands quake. What do the princes of the sea do?

cards.text: They take off their robes, strip off their embroidered garments and sit right on the ground. That's the boss walking out of the big meeting, loosening his tie and sliding right down the wall.

cards.question: True or false: The princes of the sea stay calm about Tyre's fall.

cards.text: They're clothed with terror and appalled over Tyre, trembling every moment, and I mean EVERY moment, friend. Then they lament for her.

cards.question: The princes of the sea lament over Tyre. What do they remember Tyre for?

cards.text: They say, "How you have perished, O city of renown inhabited by seafaring men". She was powerful on the sea, friend, the one name everybody had saved in their phone.

cards.question: The princes say Tyre and her people once imposed ___ on all peoples.

cards.text: The city that imposed terror on everybody, and now the coastlands tremble over HER. Then God says He'll make Tyre a desolate city like other deserted cities.

cards.question: Tyre is about to be desolate. What does God say He will raise up against her?

cards.text: The mighty waters cover her, and God brings her down with those who descend to the Pit, to dwell in the earth below like the ancient ruins. I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, friend, and even I know that's a WHOLE lot deeper.

cards.question: True or false: God says Tyre will still be set in splendor in the land of the living.
God says Tyre will be sought. What happens when people go looking for her?

cards.text: God says He'll make Tyre an object of horror, and she will be no more. The city that said "Aha!" doesn't get the last word, friend, because this message ends with "declares the Lord GOD."

findings.problem: The wrong answer "Catapults" is a 'which thing' answer, so it must be a real detail from somewhere in the Bible. Catapults don't appear in the BSB. 2 Chronicles 26:15 says only 'skillfully designed devices.' Replace it with a siege detail the BSB actually names, for example slings or fire.

rule.text: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish.

findings.problem: This story card carries three separate things: battering rams on the walls, axes on the towers, and the dust covering the city. The rams were already answered on card 2, so the card can drop them and keep the axes and the dust.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: This card only restates the answer to card 8 (they throw everything into the water). It adds nothing from the passage and doesn't move the baker forward. It could carry part of v13 instead, such as the lyres, or be cut.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to finish v13's wording ('silence the sound of your ___'). No earlier card mentions music, so there's nothing to reason from. Choosing songs over prayers or armies is luck. A story card could set up the music first, or the question could test the meaning (Tyre's celebration and music go silent).

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: Card 3 says the princes strip off their robes and sit on the ground, then compares them to a boss sliding down the wall. That rules out 'True' for the next question, "The princes of the sea stay calm about Tyre's fall," before the baker answers it.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Many cards retell God's prophecy as events happening now, in the present tense. Examples: 'Tyre becomes plunder' (stop 1 card 9), 'Nebuchadnezzar slaughters the villages' (stop 2 card 1), 'They throw it all in the WATER' (stop 2 card 9), 'The mighty waters cover her' (stop 3 card 11). In the text, every one of these is something God says He will do. Ezekiel 29:18 also notes that Nebuchadnezzar's army got no wages from Tyre, so telling the siege as a finished event can blur the line between what was prophesied and what happened. The docs say to call things what the text calls them, but they don't say whether a prophetic passage may be narrated as unfolding events.
findings.question: For prophetic passages, should Prep keep the prophecy framed as what God says will happen ("God says Nebuchadnezzar will…"), or is a present-tense storyteller retelling of the predicted events allowed?
